executive_summary.headline: Google I/O 2026 reshapes the enterprise AI stack: Gemini 3.5 Flash GA, Antigravity 2.0, Gemini Spark, and Gemini Omni all land the same week
executive_summary.body: On May 19–20, Google announced more than 100 items at I/O 2026, with four carrying immediate enterprise weight. Gemini 3.5 Flash went generally available across the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Antigravity, and Search as the new default model — outperforming Gemini 3.1 Pro on agentic and coding benchmarks at half the cost of comparable frontier models. Antigravity 2.0 launched as a standalone desktop application for orchestrating multiple agents simultaneously. Gemini Spark debuted as a 24/7 cloud-based personal AI agent running on Gemini 3.5 Flash, backed by the Antigravity harness. Gemini Omni Flash introduced a new multimodal model capable of reasoning across image, audio, text, and video to generate and edit video output. Enterprise availability for the full Gemini Enterprise suite begins rolling out immediately.

executive_summary.headline: OpenAI files confidentially for IPO at $850B+ valuation; Andrej Karpathy joins Anthropic
executive_summary.body: On May 20, CNBC and WSJ confirmed that OpenAI submitted a confidential draft IPO prospectus to regulators, working with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley toward a potential public debut in Q4 2026 at a valuation above $850 billion — making it one of the largest public offerings in history if completed. The same day, Anthropic announced that Andrej Karpathy, a co-founder of OpenAI and former Tesla AI director, joined Anthropic's pre-training team to help accelerate Claude's core training research. Both moves signal a week of significant structural shifts at frontier labs beyond product releases.

executive_summary.headline: Hark raises $700M Series A at $6B valuation to build a universal AI interface and hardware platform
executive_summary.body: On May 21, Brett Adcock — founder of Figure AI and Archer Aviation — disclosed that his newest company Hark closed a $700 million Series A led by Parkway Venture Capital and including Nvidia, AMD Ventures, Intel Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, ARK Invest, and Brookfield, valuing the company at $6 billion post-money. Hark is building models and hardware for an agentic AI system designed to act as a universal interface with the digital world, with first multimodal models expected this summer and hardware devices to follow. The round is the largest Series A in AI for 2026 and signals intense investor conviction that consumer-facing agentic hardware is the next major platform.

executive_summary.headline: Kore.ai launches Artemis and NVIDIA delivers the first Vera CPUs — enterprise AI infrastructure accelerates
executive_summary.body: Kore.ai launched its Artemis platform on May 21, introducing the Agent Blueprint Language (ABL) — a compiled, declarative YAML-based standard that lets enterprises define, validate, and govern multi-agent systems — with deep Microsoft Azure integration and support for 175 AI models. The same week, NVIDIA delivered the first production units of its Vera CPU — 88 custom Olympus cores, 1.2TB/s memory bandwidth, 2x energy efficiency of traditional infrastructure — to Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure on May 18–19. The Vera CPU is NVIDIA's first silicon designed specifically for agentic AI workloads: sandboxes, tool calls, orchestration layers, and long-context retrieval. OCI will deploy hundreds of thousands of Vera CPUs beginning in 2026.

executive_summary.headline: Anthropic acquires Stainless for SDK and MCP server tooling; Google CodeMender integrates into Agent Platform
executive_summary.body: On May 18, Anthropic announced the acquisition of Stainless, a startup that has generated every official Anthropic SDK since the earliest days of the API and is used by hundreds of companies to produce TypeScript, Python, Go, Java SDKs, CLIs, and MCP servers from API specifications. No purchase price was disclosed. The acquisition reflects Anthropic's recognition that agent connectivity — not just model intelligence — determines real-world utility. Also during the week, Google announced that CodeMender, its AI security agent from DeepMind, is being integrated into the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and will be available soon to enterprise customers for autonomous vulnerability identification, patch generation, testing, and remediation.

top_picks.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash — General Availability
top_picks.subtitle: Google's agentic-first model: frontier coding and agent performance, 1M token context, 4x faster than comparable models

secondary_urls.label: Gemini 3.5 Flash model card — Google DeepMind
Simon Willison pricing and benchmark analysis

top_picks.summary: Gemini 3.5 Flash reached general availability on May 19 across the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Antigravity, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and the Gemini app — and immediately became the default model in AI Mode in Search globally. It outperforms Gemini 3.1 Pro on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (76.2%), GDPval-AA (1,656 Elo), and MCP Atlas (83.6%), leads multimodal understanding on CharXiv (84.2%), and generates output four times faster than comparable frontier models. Pricing is $1.50 per million input tokens and $9.00 per million output tokens with a 90% cached-input discount. Gemini 3.5 Pro is in internal testing and expected to roll out next month.
top_picks.competitive_context: Gemini 3.5 Flash is designed explicitly for agentic workflows — terminal-level task execution, multi-step coding, and long-context reasoning — rather than general-purpose chat. At $1.50/$9.00 per million tokens with a 90% cache discount, it undercuts GPT-5.5's comparable tiers on cost-per-agent-task. Shopify, Macquarie Bank, Salesforce, Ramp, Xero, and Databricks are named production users at launch. The simultaneous availability through Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform means enterprise teams can access the model inside Google's managed security boundary without separate procurement.
top_picks.pricing: $1.50 per million input tokens, $9.00 per million output tokens, 90% discount on cached inputs. Available via Gemini API and Gemini Enterprise (enterprise pricing through Google Cloud contract).
key_takeaways: Gemini 3.5 Flash is Google's strongest agentic and coding model yet — it outperforms Gemini 3.1 Pro on agentic benchmarks while operating faster and, at scale, cheaper.
The 1M token context window enables long-horizon enterprise workflows such as full-codebase analysis, multi-document financial reconciliation, and 100+ page contract review.
Xero's deployment for autonomous 1099 tax-form workflows and Macquarie Bank's 100+ page document reasoning are verified production use cases, not pilot claims.
The 90% cache discount is material for enterprise agents that repeatedly process the same large system prompt or document corpus — a pattern common in regulated workflow automation.
Gemini 3.5 Pro rollout next month will bring additional capability headroom; enterprise teams should evaluate 3.5 Flash now and track 3.5 Pro for high-complexity tasks.

top_picks.title: Google Antigravity 2.0 — Standalone Desktop Agent Development Platform
top_picks.subtitle: Desktop app, CLI, and SDK for orchestrating multiple AI agents simultaneously; enterprise Cloud connector launching
top_picks.summary: Google launched Antigravity 2.0 at I/O 2026 as a standalone desktop application for agent-first development, replacing the prior web-only Gemini CLI surface. The app lets users orchestrate multiple agents in parallel, design custom subagent workflows, and schedule background tasks. A new Antigravity CLI serves terminal-first developers; the Antigravity SDK gives programmatic access to the same harness. Google Cloud customers can now connect their Cloud projects directly to Antigravity. Enterprise customers gain custom agent templates in AI Studio. Google reduced the AI Ultra plan from $250 to $200 (20x higher limits than Pro) and introduced a new $100 AI Ultra tier (5x higher limits than Pro).
top_picks.competitive_context: Antigravity 2.0 is Google's direct answer to Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex — but it competes on orchestration depth rather than coding speed. The key differentiator is the multi-agent parallel orchestration capability and the SDK that allows enterprises to host custom agents on their own infrastructure. The Gemini CLI migration path is explicit: Google asked existing Gemini CLI users to move to Antigravity CLI, consolidating the developer surface. Enterprise Antigravity access through Gemini Enterprise begins rolling out in the coming months.
top_picks.pricing: Antigravity is included in Google AI Pro ($20/month), a new AI Ultra tier ($100/month, 5x higher limits than Pro), and the existing AI Ultra ($200/month, reduced from $250, 20x limits). Enterprise access via Gemini Enterprise Cloud contract pricing.
key_takeaways: The Antigravity SDK allows enterprises to host custom agents on their own infrastructure — a critical governance option for regulated organizations that cannot allow agent workloads to run on Google's cloud.
Parallel subagent orchestration is the functional breakthrough: Antigravity demonstrated a two-agent synthesis of the AlphaZero paper and code for a fully playable game in six hours.
Google Cloud customers can now connect Antigravity to their Cloud projects directly — teams already in Google Cloud can access agentic development without a separate tool relationship.
Custom agent templates for enterprise users in AI Studio lower the barrier for enterprise teams to prototype agents before committing to production architecture.
Migration from Gemini CLI is explicit — teams using Gemini CLI for agent tasks should prioritize evaluating Antigravity CLI this quarter.

top_picks.title: Hark — $700M Series A at $6B Valuation
top_picks.subtitle: Brett Adcock building universal AI interface and hardware; multimodal models expected summer 2026
top_picks.summary: Hark, an AI lab building models and hardware for a universal agentic AI interface, closed a $700 million Series A led by Parkway Venture Capital — the largest Series A in AI for 2026. Investors include Nvidia, AMD Ventures, Intel Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, ARK Invest, Prime Movers Lab, Brookfield, and Greycroft. The company, founded in late 2025 by Brett Adcock with $100 million of his own capital, plans to release first multimodal models this summer and follow with dedicated hardware devices. Post-money valuation is $6 billion. No product has been publicly released.
top_picks.competitive_context: The Hark round follows a pattern established by Perplexity's hardware ambitions and OpenAI's device aspirations — frontier lab capital flowing toward hardware-plus-model combined plays. Nvidia and both major CPU chip vendors (AMD, Intel, Qualcomm) co-investing signals hardware partnership discussions underway. Adcock's prior companies (Figure AI robots, Archer Aviation) demonstrate a track record of building hardware-intensive deep tech. The 'universal interface' framing positions Hark against Apple's forthcoming AI-native Siri and Google's Gemini Spark — but from a hardware-first starting point.
top_picks.pricing: No product or pricing available at time of this writing. First multimodal models expected summer 2026.
key_takeaways: At $6B valuation pre-product, the round prices Hark on Adcock's track record and chip-vendor partnership terms, not revenue — making this ADD TO WATCHLIST, not EVALUATE NOW.
Chip-company co-investors (Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Qualcomm) suggest hardware supply agreements are structurally embedded in the financing, not merely strategic bets.
The 'universal interface' vision directly competes with Apple, Google, and OpenAI's hardware ambitions — watch for summer model release as the first real signal of differentiation.
Salesforce Ventures as co-investor suggests Hark's platform could integrate with enterprise CRM and workflow software from day one.
Enterprise teams do not need to act now but should queue Hark for evaluation when models release this summer.

top_picks.title: Kore.ai Artemis — Enterprise Agent Platform with Agent Blueprint Language
top_picks.subtitle: ABL compiled agentic standard, Dual-Brain Architecture, deep Azure integration; 175 model support
top_picks.summary: Kore.ai launched Artemis — its new enterprise agent platform — introducing Agent Blueprint Language (ABL), a compiled declarative YAML-based standard for defining, validating, and governing multi-agent systems. The platform's Dual-Brain Architecture runs a reasoning LLM and a deterministic business-rules engine in parallel through shared memory. Arch, the platform's AI orchestration layer, translates business requirements into production-ready ABL, deploys, monitors, and self-optimizes agents. Artemis is available today on Microsoft Azure with deep integration into Microsoft Foundry, Agent 365, Entra ID, and Microsoft Graph. It supports 175 AI models, 40+ voice and digital channels, and 300+ enterprise integrations. Kore.ai reports $100M ARR and 450 million daily interactions automated.
top_picks.competitive_context: Artemis positions against Salesforce Agentforce (CRM-native), Microsoft Copilot Studio (M365-native), and ServiceNow (ITSM-native). Kore.ai's differentiator is vendor neutrality — Artemis runs across Azure, AWS, GCP, and on-premises while integrating natively into Microsoft's stack, a combination the pure-play Microsoft-shop platforms cannot match. The Dual-Brain Architecture's deterministic rule-engine layer is the governance answer for regulated industries where pure LLM decision-making is too opaque. 75% of Kore.ai's existing customer base is in regulated industries, which aligns with an enterprise AI team operating in a governed, public-company environment.
top_picks.pricing: Custom enterprise pricing. No public rate card. ABL runtime not yet available as a standalone component; lighter version planned.
key_takeaways: ABL as a compiled, version-controlled agent standard is the governance primitive missing from most enterprise AI platforms — agents can be stored in GitHub, reviewed in CI/CD pipelines, and audited like code.

The Dual-Brain Architecture gives regulated industry teams a deterministic fallback layer: when the LLM output needs to be locked to a specific business rule, the rules engine takes over without model substitution.
Deep Microsoft integration (Foundry, Agent 365, Entra, Graph) makes Artemis a credible option for Microsoft-shop enterprises that need multi-cloud or on-premises agent governance.
The 75% regulated-industry customer base and Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader status validate production readiness at scale, not just benchmark claims.
Enterprise teams evaluating agentic platforms should run a comparative assessment of Artemis against Copilot Studio for regulated, multi-cloud workflows before Q3 budget cycles.

top_picks.title: NVIDIA Vera CPU — First Production Deliveries
top_picks.subtitle: 88 Olympus cores, 1.2TB/s memory bandwidth, purpose-built for agentic workloads; OCI to deploy at hyperscale
top_picks.summary: On May 18–19, NVIDIA hand-delivered the first production units of its Vera CPU to Anthropic (San Francisco), OpenAI (Mission Bay), SpaceXAI (Palo Alto), and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (Santa Clara). Vera is NVIDIA's first custom CPU, designed specifically for agentic AI workloads — orchestration layers, tool calls, long-context retrieval, and agent sandboxes. It packs 88 custom Olympus cores with 50% faster single-threaded performance, 1.2TB/s memory bandwidth, and 2x energy efficiency versus traditional infrastructure. OCI will deploy hundreds of thousands of Vera CPUs beginning in 2026 and is the first cloud provider to offer Vera-powered infrastructure at hyperscale.
top_picks.competitive_context: Vera is NVIDIA's explicit acknowledgment that agentic AI has a CPU bottleneck — GPU scaling no longer fully captures the value. Intel and AMD are the incumbent competition for CPU infrastructure, both of which co-invested in Hark this week — a possible signal they are hedging against NVIDIA's CPU expansion. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's hyperscale Vera deployment (hundreds of thousands of units) gives OCI a near-term differentiated infrastructure position for customers running large-scale agentic workloads. AWS, Azure, and GCP Vera deployments were not announced and are not yet publicly confirmed.
top_picks.pricing: Not separately priced for end customers. Available through OCI compute infrastructure; enterprise pricing via Oracle Cloud contract.
key_takeaways: Vera is not a GPU story — it is NVIDIA's answer to the CPU bottleneck in production agentic systems where orchestration, tool calls, and retrieval dominate compute cost.
OCI's first-mover position on Vera at hyperscale gives Oracle Cloud a concrete infrastructure differentiator for enterprise customers scaling agentic deployments.
Teams designing production multi-agent infrastructure should account for Vera as an option in OCI over the next two to three quarters.
AMD and Intel co-investing in Hark while Vera ships is worth tracking as a chip-industry signal about which companies are treating agentic CPUs as a strategic category.
No action required for most enterprise teams today, but infrastructure architects planning 2027 cloud contracts should include OCI in their agentic compute evaluation.

top_picks.title: Anthropic Acquires Stainless — SDK and MCP Server Tooling
top_picks.subtitle: The startup behind all official Anthropic SDKs joins to advance Claude's agent connectivity layer
top_picks.summary: Anthropic announced the acquisition of Stainless on May 18. Stainless generates SDKs across TypeScript, Python, Go, and Java, CLIs, and MCP servers from API specifications, and has powered every official Anthropic SDK since the earliest days of the Claude API. Hundreds of companies use Stainless for their own SDK and MCP server generation. No deal terms were disclosed. The acquisition is framed as a strategic move to improve Claude's connectivity to external tools and data sources — reflecting Anthropic's view that agents are only as capable as the systems they can reach.
top_picks.competitive_context: The acquisition signals that MCP server generation — converting an enterprise API spec into a Claude-ready connector — is about to get significantly faster and more polished. Companies that today spend engineering time building MCP connectors manually may soon get auto-generated ones from Anthropic tooling. This is a direct attack on the integration middleware category (Zapier, MuleSoft, Workato) that has historically owned enterprise API connectivity. For development teams using Claude Code, expect improved SDK reliability and faster connector publishing in the next few quarters.
top_picks.pricing: No change to Claude API pricing; Stainless's commercial products may be integrated into the Claude developer tooling suite.
key_takeaways: Every official Anthropic SDK was already built by Stainless — this acquisition internalizes that capability and gives Anthropic direct control over developer experience across TypeScript, Python, Go, and Java.
MCP server auto-generation from API specs is the capability that will lower enterprise integration friction — turning a multi-week custom connector project into a single spec submission.
Development teams building Claude integrations should watch the Anthropic documentation channel for updated SDK releases that may reflect Stainless improvements within the next 1–2 quarters.
The deal is a direct challenge to middleware platforms — if Anthropic ships MCP server generation at scale, the value of hand-built integration layers shrinks.
Hundreds of companies using Stainless externally will need clarity on product continuity; Anthropic has not yet published a transition roadmap.

top_picks.title: Gemini Spark — 24/7 Personal AI Agent
top_picks.subtitle: Cloud-based agent running Gemini 3.5 Flash on Antigravity harness; works while your laptop is closed

secondary_urls.label: Google Cloud enterprise Gemini Spark details

top_picks.summary: Google introduced Gemini Spark at I/O 2026 as a 24/7 personal AI agent powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash and the Antigravity harness. Spark runs in the cloud and continues executing tasks after a laptop is closed or a phone is locked. It integrates deeply with Gmail, Docs, Slides, and through MCP connections to Canva, OpenTable, Instacart, and expanding partner apps. In the Gemini Enterprise context, Spark connects to Microsoft SharePoint, OneDrive, ServiceNow, and Salesforce with approval-gated actions. Every task runs in a fresh, isolated ephemeral VM; DLP enforcement applies through the Agent Gateway. Rolling out to trusted testers this week; Beta for U.S. Google AI Ultra subscribers next week.
top_picks.competitive_context: Gemini Spark is Google's direct answer to the Siri evolution Apple previewed for WWDC 2026 and to OpenAI's Personal AI agent roadmap. The key enterprise differentiator is the ephemeral VM isolation model — each Spark task runs in a clean environment with no persistent state leakage between tasks, backed by Google Cloud security guarantees. Enterprise teams running Gemini Enterprise gain Spark with Salesforce and ServiceNow connectors, which positions this as an agent layer over the existing SaaS stack rather than a replacement. The Beta timeline (Ultra subscribers next week) means enterprise evaluation data will be available within a month.
top_picks.pricing: Included in Google AI Ultra ($100/month new tier or $200/month reduced from $250). Enterprise access through Gemini Enterprise — pricing via Google Cloud contract.
key_takeaways: Background task execution (continues when laptop is closed) changes the architectural assumption that agents need human supervision at all times — enterprises should evaluate the governance implications of persistent background agents.
Approval-gated actions (Spark asks before sending emails or spending money) are the compliance primitive — ensure this is the default configuration in any enterprise deployment.

MCP connections to Salesforce and ServiceNow inside Gemini Enterprise mean Spark could automate cross-system workflows (e.g., escalating a ServiceNow incident by updating a Salesforce account) without custom integration code.
The ephemeral VM isolation model is the trust boundary story for regulated enterprises — each task is stateless by default, which satisfies audit requirements that persistent agent sessions cannot.
ADD TO WATCHLIST: wait for the Beta to ship to Ultra subscribers next week, then run a controlled evaluation of a single, well-bounded workflow before enabling broader deployment.

items.title: LobeHub
items.subtitle: Chief Agent Operator — multi-agent orchestration via Slack, Discord, Telegram, iMessage
items.summary: LobeHub is a Chief Agent Operator (CAO) that builds, runs, and coordinates AI agent teams in the cloud. Describe a goal; it assembles the right agents and skills, runs tasks in parallel, routes work across models, and reports back only when decisions are needed — delivered via existing channels (Slack, Discord, Telegram, iMessage). 460 upvotes, #1 on May 18.

items.title: StoreClaw
items.subtitle: AI growth engine for e-commerce: operations, SEO, social content, channel performance — #1 Product of the Day
items.summary: StoreClaw is an AI agent platform for e-commerce operators. It monitors orders, inventory, and conversion rates, diagnoses shifts, generates a month of social content, and tracks performance across Amazon, Shopify, Wix, and TikTok Shop in one place. Achieved #1 Product of the Day on Product Hunt on May 21. Launching with 300 free credits for new users.

items.title: Gemini Omni
items.subtitle: Create anything from any input — starting with video; #11 on weekly leaderboard
items.summary: Gemini Omni Flash is the first model in Google's new Omni multimodal family, capable of reasoning across image, audio, video, and text to generate and edit videos — not just stitch inputs together. Available now in the Gemini app, YouTube Shorts, and Google Flow. API access coming in the coming weeks. All generated videos carry SynthID watermarks. Avatar generation requires an identity-verification onboarding step to prevent deepfakes.

items.title: Stitch 3.0 by Google
items.subtitle: Generate and iterate UI screens with AI on a live canvas; #14 on weekly leaderboard
items.summary: Stitch 3.0 adds real-time design steering via text or speech, import of existing codebases and design files, and live canvas iteration for UI generation. Launched at Google I/O 2026 as part of Google's generative UI push. Free to use for developers with a Google account.

items.title: TestSprite 3.0
items.subtitle: Fleet of parallel AI agents tests your app in minutes; #7 on weekly leaderboard
items.summary: TestSprite 3.0 deploys a fleet of parallel AI agents to test web apps autonomously in minutes. The platform handles end-to-end test creation, execution, and failure reporting without requiring developers to write test cases manually. Positioned as a drop-in replacement for Playwright or Cypress with zero configuration.

items.title: Composer 2.5
items.subtitle: Cursor's most powerful model yet — trading, coding agent; #8 on weekly leaderboard
items.summary: Composer 2.5 is described on Product Hunt as 'Cursor's most powerful model yet' — suggesting a coding-agent system compatible with or positioned against the Cursor IDE. The description references AI-driven trading and coding capabilities. Limited public information at time of writing; enterprise relevance is low given the consumer/trader framing.

items.title: PollyReach
items.subtitle: Give your AI agent a real phone number and voice for outbound calls; #2 on weekly leaderboard
items.summary: PollyReach provides AI voice agents with real phone numbers to make outbound calls autonomously. Targets sales automation, customer outreach, and service follow-up workflows. Integrates with existing CRM systems via webhooks. 437 upvotes, #2 on May 18.

items.title: Mintlify Workflows
items.subtitle: Self-updating knowledge bases that stay current automatically; #15 on weekly leaderboard
items.summary: Mintlify Workflows adds automation that keeps documentation and knowledge bases self-updating as codebases and APIs evolve. Designed to eliminate documentation drift — a persistent pain point for enterprise developer portals and internal wikis. Integrates with existing Mintlify docs setup.

Outperforms Gemini 3.1 Pro on terminal tasks, coding, and MCP agent benchmarks. $1.50/$9.00 per million tokens with 90% cache discount. See Top Picks for complete evaluation.

items.title: Gemini Omni Flash
items.subtitle: Multimodal world model: reasoning across image, audio, video, and text for video generation and editing
items.summary: Gemini Omni Flash is the first model in Google's new Omni family — a multimodal model that reasons across image, audio, text, and video inputs to produce video output, including physics-aware generation, cultural and historical context, and conversational editing. Available now in Gemini app, YouTube Shorts, and Google Flow for AI Pro/Ultra subscribers. Enterprise API access coming in weeks. All output carries SynthID watermarks. Omni Pro model with higher capability is planned.

items.title: Ettin Reranker Family — Hugging Face
items.subtitle: Six open-source rerankers from 17M to 1B parameters; Apache 2.0; matches teacher at 2.4x speed
items.summary: Hugging Face released the Ettin Reranker Family — six open-source cross-encoder rerankers (17M, 32M, 68M, 140M, 400M, 1B parameters) trained via distillation on the mxbai-rerank-large-v2 teacher. The 1B model closely matches its 1.54B teacher on MTEB retrieval benchmarks (0.6114 vs 0.6115) while running 2.4x faster. All six released under Apache 2.0. Built on JHU's ModernBERT-style Ettin encoder architecture with support for up to 8,192 token context. Relevant for enterprise RAG pipelines where reranking quality determines answer accuracy.

items.title: OpenAI Offering $2M in API Credits to Every YC S26 Company
items.subtitle: YC S26 deadline extended to May 25; OpenAI uncapped SAFE structure mirrors Airbnb/Stripe model
items.summary: On May 20, YC announced that OpenAI will provide $2 million in API credits to every company in the YC Spring 2025 and Summer 2026 batches, structured as an uncapped SAFE — the same financing vehicle used in early-stage partnerships with Airbnb and Stripe. YC extended the S26 application deadline to May 25. The in-person S26 program runs July–September 2026 in San Francisco. This positions OpenAI as the default API provider for the S26 cohort at the most critical early stage of product development.

items.subtitle: OpenAI co-founder returns to frontier R&D on Claude's core training; will lead a new AI-accelerated pre-training research team
items.summary: Andrej Karpathy announced on May 19 that he has joined Anthropic, where he will work on the pre-training team under lead Nick Joseph and build a new team focused on using Claude to accelerate pre-training research. Karpathy co-founded OpenAI and previously directed AI at Tesla. Pre-training is the large-scale training process that gives Claude its core knowledge and capabilities — one of the most compute-intensive phases of frontier model development.

items.title: Google CodeMender Integrates into Agent Platform
items.subtitle: Autonomous code security agent — vulnerability identification, patch generation, test, and remediation — coming to Gemini Enterprise

secondary_urls.label: InfoWorld deep-dive on Agent Platform integration

items.summary: Google announced at I/O 2026 that CodeMender — a DeepMind-developed AI security agent — is being integrated into the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and will be available to enterprise customers soon. CodeMender autonomously identifies vulnerabilities in code, recommends precise fixes, securely tests them in isolation, and applies patches with user approval. It was originally developed by Google DeepMind and launched in limited API preview at I/O 2026. Google positioned it as a direct competitor to Anthropic's Mythos security agent.

items.title: Google Search Agents and Information Agents in AI Mode
items.subtitle: 24/7 background information agents, generative UI in Search, Gemini 3.5 Flash as default — the biggest Search upgrade in 25 years
items.summary: Google announced at I/O 2026 that Search has passed 1 billion monthly AI Mode users and is upgrading the Search box with Gemini 3.5 Flash as the default model globally. New features include: 24/7 background Information Agents (launching first for Google AI Pro/Ultra subscribers this summer) that monitor the web and specific data sources; generative UI in Search that builds custom visual tools, simulations, and dashboards on the fly (free for everyone this summer); and a redesigned Search box described as the biggest upgrade in over 25 years.

items.summary: Kore.ai launched Artemis with Agent Blueprint Language and Dual-Brain Architecture on May 21. See Top Picks for complete evaluation.

items.title: WebMCP — Proposed Open Web Standard for Browser Agents
items.subtitle: Google proposes structured tool API for browser-based agents; available as Chrome flag, origin trial in Chrome 149
items.summary: Google published the WebMCP specification on May 18 as a proposed open web standard that allows web pages to expose structured tools — defined via JavaScript (Imperative API) or HTML form annotations (Declarative API) — to browser-based AI agents. Tools can include checkout flows, filter actions, support form navigation, and diagnostic functions. Available as a Chrome flag for local development; entering origin trial in Chrome 149. The goal is to reduce brittle DOM-scraping by AI agents and provide agents with reliable, permission-controlled access to site capabilities.

items.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Hub — New Experience
items.subtitle: Prompt Gallery, AI Council page, redesigned adoption resources — launched May 18
items.summary: Microsoft released a redesigned Microsoft 365 Copilot Hub on May 18 including a new Prompt Gallery, a guide for creating an AI Council within an organization, and a feedback guide for Copilot Champions. The Hub includes a Build Agents with Microsoft 365 Copilot resource page and updated Copilot Studio community links. This is adoption and governance tooling, not a model release — but it signals Microsoft's focus on operationalizing enterprise Copilot rollouts through structured governance structures.

items.title: OpenAI Confidential IPO Filing
items.subtitle: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley; $850B+ valuation; Q4 2026 target public debut
items.summary: OpenAI submitted a confidential draft IPO prospectus as early as Friday May 23, working with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, with a Q4 2026 target for public debut. Current private valuation is above $850 billion. If completed as the world's most valuable AI company, this would be among the largest IPOs in history. No term sheet finalized; CNBC confirmed the filing on May 20.

sections.title: Open Source & Dev Tool Releases

items.title: Ettin Reranker Family (HuggingFace)
items.subtitle: Six Apache 2.0 rerankers, 17M–1B params; 1B model matches 1.54B teacher at 2.4x speed
items.summary: Hugging Face released the Ettin Reranker Family — six open-source, Apache 2.0 cross-encoder rerankers trained via distillation on mxbai-rerank-large-v2. The 1B model achieves parity with its 1.54B teacher on MTEB retrieval (0.6114 vs 0.6115) while running 2.4x faster. All models support up to 8,192 token context. Built on the ModernBERT-style Ettin encoder from Johns Hopkins University. Immediately deployable for enterprise RAG pipeline reranking without licensing restrictions.

items.title: WebMCP Open Standard
items.subtitle: Google-proposed open web standard for structured browser-agent tool APIs; see Enterprise AI section
items.summary: Google proposed WebMCP as an open web standard for exposing structured tools to browser-based AI agents. Available as a Chrome flag in Chrome 149 origin trial. See Enterprise AI section for full coverage.

items.title: Antigravity CLI and SDK — Open Developer Access
items.subtitle: Google opens Antigravity harness to third-party builders; host agents on own infrastructure
items.summary: Google launched the Antigravity CLI for terminal-first developers and the Antigravity SDK for programmatic access to the same agent harness powering Google's products. Builders can customize agent behavior and host on their own infrastructure — a critical option for regulated organizations that cannot run agentic workloads on Google's cloud. Available today to all developers with a Google account.

items.title: Gemini 3.5 Pro — Confirmed for Next Month
items.subtitle: Already in internal use at Google; planned rollout within weeks of 3.5 Flash GA
items.summary: Google confirmed at I/O 2026 that Gemini 3.5 Pro is already in internal use and will roll out next month. Given 3.5 Flash's outperformance of 3.1 Pro on agentic benchmarks, 3.5 Pro is expected to establish a new frontier capability ceiling for complex, long-horizon enterprise workflows. No pricing, benchmarks, or specific date disclosed beyond 'next month.'

items.title: Google Managed Agents API (Beta)
items.subtitle: Single API call provisions a remote Linux environment with Gemini 3.5 Flash — tool calls, code execution, file management
items.summary: Google launched the Managed Agents API in beta via the Gemini API. A single API call provisions a remote Linux environment where an agent can reason, plan, call tools, execute code, manage files in an isolated sandbox, and browse the web for live data. Powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash and the Antigravity harness. Available in Google AI Studio and via the Interactions API today. Inherits Agent Platform enterprise data privacy and governance protections.

items.title: SAP Joule Studio — GA for Building Enterprise Agents
items.subtitle: Free design-time access through end of 2026; MCP and A2A support; GA expected Q3 2026
items.summary: SAP announced Joule Studio at Sapphire 2026 as its AI-first, fully managed development environment for building enterprise agents and agentic workflows. Free design-time access (including AI-assisted development under fair-use limits) through end of 2026. Supports MCP and A2A interoperability. GA expected Q3 2026. Relevant for organizations running SAP ERP who want to build agents inside the SAP ecosystem without starting from a blank-slate platform.

flagged_unverified.claim: Anthropic raised $30B at $900B valuation — closed during May 18-24 week
flagged_unverified.reason: Bloomberg and WSJ reported as of May 12 that Anthropic was 'in talks' for a $30B round at ~$900B valuation. As of May 24, no company announcement or confirmed close. The YouTube AI update from May 22 mentioned '$30B at $900B' as if closed, but no primary source (Anthropic press release or SEC filing) confirms the round closed during this specific week. Excluded from funding section to avoid premature reporting.
